title: P1.7-pre-f Make the control-room client root browser-loadable
description: Production prerequisite discovered by the real P1.7 Playwright lane at tracked HEAD bda564a8. The Cordum v2 dev UI imports @moe/control-room-client; its package root statically re-exports contract-digest.ts, which imports createHash from node:crypto. Vite dev externalizes node:crypto and browser evaluation throws before React mounts: `Module "node:crypto" has been externalized for browser compatibility. Cannot access "node:crypto.createHash" in client code.` The production build happens to tree-shake the module and exits 0 with a warning, so build-only coverage misses the live defect. Deliver the smallest browser-safe package boundary while retaining one authoritative contract digest derivation for generator and release tooling. This row unblocks task-965cb2d669a24df49b750b6c59114697 step 2; do not mask the defect with a Playwright/Vite polyfill.
definitionOfDone: A committed real-browser regression arm loads the Cordum v2 entry through the Vite development module graph and reaches its production shell; it fails before the fix on the exact node:crypto/createHash page error and passes after. The arm must prove it executed with a nonzero Playwright test count.

No module reachable from the browser-facing @moe/control-room-client root imports a Node builtin. If contract digest derivation remains a root export it is genuinely browser-safe; if it moves to an explicit Node-only subpath, update every tracked generator/release consumer and the exact root-export roster without a deep relative import.

Generator and release-subject callers still derive the same 64-hex digest from canonicalContractSurface, and GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST remains equal. Any replacement hash implementation is pinned by independent standard SHA-256 vectors, not only a generated constant derived by the same implementation.

The production Vite build and Vite dev browser lane both succeed without a node:crypto externalization warning/error attributable to @moe/control-room-client. Package typecheck and focused tests run with nonzero counts.
Mutation evidence proves the browser arm goes red when the Node-only import/root re-export is restored, while digest equality and release-subject arms stay independently green or red as appropriate.
taskRails: Do not solve this in test configuration, via a browser polyfill, or by weakening/removing contract digest authority. The production package boundary must itself be browser-loadable.
Preserve the single-source relationship among canonicalContractSurface, generated pins, and release subject; do not hand-copy a digest literal into a second authority.
Re-measure live ownership of contract-digest, package index/export roster, generator and release-subject paths before editing; preserve foreign WIP and commit explicit paths only.

implementationPlan.description:
ADD THE DAEMON-FREE VITE DEV LANE PORT. Create `tests/e2e/control-room/dev-graph-ports.ts`.

WHY A NEW MODULE RATHER THAN REUSE. The only existing dev-server starter is module-private inside `tests/e2e/control-room/daemon-ports.ts`, bundled with a daemon boot and a demo seed, and that file is FOREIGN WIP owned by task-965cb2d6 (tracked modification, pinned at exactly 300 lines). Epic rail 1 forbids disturbing it, and a daemon adds ~60s plus a second failure surface that could mask the module-graph error this arm exists to catch.

SHAPE (mirror `static-ports.ts` / `harness.ts` conventions; target <=250 lines, hard split before 400):
- Import ONLY from the clean tracked helpers: `spawnNode`, `watch`, `freePort`, `killTree` from `./daemon-children.js`; `repoRoot`, `serverEnv` from `./daemon-scratch.js`.
- Export a frozen `DEV_GRAPH_ERROR_CODES` tuple and its derived type. At minimum: `E2E_REPO_ROOT_UNRESOLVED`, `E2E_DEV_SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT`. Every refusal carries a STABLE reason code plus the child's trailing transcript, never a bare boolean.
- Export `withDevGraphControlRoom<T>(body: (baseUrl: string) => Promise<T>): Promise<LaneOutcome<T>>` returning `{ok:true,value}` or `{ok:false,code,detail}` — so a run that never reached the body cannot read as a pass.
- Launch: `spawnNode([`${root}/apps/control-room/node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js`, "--port", String(port), "--strictPort"], `${root}/apps/control-room`, serverEnv("http://127.0.0.1:1", "ABSENT"))`. The dead daemon origin and ABSENT credentials are deliberate: this arm certifies the MODULE GRAPH, not a connected system.
- Readiness: wait for stdout matching `/Local:\s+(http:\/\/localhost:\d+)/u` within a bounded budget (60_000ms), and refuse `E2E_DEV_SERVER_READY_TIMEOUT` with the transcript tail if it does not arrive. Assert the announced origin equals the requested port; a different port is a second server this lane does not own.
- Teardown: `killTree` in a `finally`, on EVERY exit path — success, thrown assertion, readiness timeout (R5).

Gate this step with `pnpm exec tsc -p tests/e2e/control-room/tsconfig.json` (standalone, unpiped, exit 0).

- Assert BOTH, because either alone can pass for the wrong reason (R1):

- Do NOT assert an empty console: with no daemon the handshake fetch legitimately fails (R4).
- Assert the lane outcome equals `{ok:true, value: ...}` so a refusal cannot read as a pass.

RED EVIDENCE (required, quote verbatim): `pnpm exec playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts dev-module-graph.spec.ts` — standalone, unpiped. Must print `Running 1 test using 1 worker`, exit NONZERO, and the failure must name the exact string `Module "node:crypto" has been externalized for browser compatibility. Cannot access "node:crypto.createHash" in client code.` A red with any OTHER reason means the arm is measuring something else — fix the arm, do not proceed.

DIVERGENCE RECORD (epic rail 7A, required, R2). At this SAME red tree also run `pnpm exec playwright test -c tests/e2e/control-room/playwright.config.ts control-room-smoke.spec.ts` and quote its PASSING count line. That pass is the point: the pre-existing static-bundle fence is green on the broken tree because the production bundler tree-shakes the unused digest module, so it cannot refuse this defect. Recording both outcomes at one tree is what distinguishes the new arm from the fence that already existed. Post both transcripts as a task comment.

THREE options were weighed.

(A) CHOSEN — move the digest off the browser-facing root onto an explicit Node-only subpath. `contract-digest.ts` is left BYTE-IDENTICAL (one authority, `createHash` retained), only its reachability changes: delete `index.ts:2`, declare `"./contract-digest": "./src/contract-digest.ts"` in the package `exports` map, repoint the single external consumer. (B) REJECTED — keep the digest on the root and replace `node:crypto.createHash` with a hand-rolled pure-JS SHA-256 (DoD item 2's first branch; DoD item 3's independent-vector sentence anticipates it). Disclosed as a follow-up, not taken here, per the DELIVERY BIAS rail.

DoD-item-2 AMBIGUITY, resolved by measurement, disclosed for QA. The clause reads "...update every tracked generator/release consumer and the exact root-export roster without a deep relative import." planningNotes.risks:
R1 — THE ARM CAN PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON (epic rail 7A divergence). A spec that only asserts "the shell element exists" would also go green under a Vite polyfill or an unrelated change, and task rail 1 forbids exactly that fix. The arm must therefore assert TWO things that can only both hold after a real boundary fix: (a) `cr2.shell.root` has count 1, AND (b) the collected page-error/console-error set contains NOTHING matching /node:crypto|externalized for browser compatibility/u. Assert the CAPTURED-ERROR SET explicitly, not merely the absence of a throw.

R2 — THE SHARED FENCE THAT CANNOT SEE THIS DEFECT. `control-room-smoke.spec.ts` looks like an identical browser fence but runs `vite build` + a static server, and the production bundler TREE-SHAKES the unused digest module, so it is GREEN on the broken tree. That is the divergence this plan requires the worker to record in step 2: at the RED tree, the new dev arm FAILS while the static smoke PASSES. Without that record, a grader cannot tell the new arm from the one that already existed.

R3 — PAGE ERROR MUST BE CAPTURED BEFORE NAVIGATION. `mem:gotcha-control-room-client-node-crypto-vite-dev`: subscribe `page.on("pageerror")` and `page.on("console")` BEFORE `page.goto`, or the throw happens during module evaluation and is lost, and the failure then reads as a UI/pairing timeout instead of a module-graph error. Race the collected errors against the shell locator; do not wait for a 180s timeout to learn what already failed in 2 seconds.

R4 — NO DAEMON IS ATTACHED, DELIBERATELY. The plain route fires a handshake `fetch` that will fail. That is a NETWORK failure, not a page error, and must not red the arm. Filter the asserted error set to the node:crypto signature; do not assert an empty console.

R5 — RESOURCE CLEANUP. The dev server is a spawned child. Kill the tree on EVERY exit path (success, assertion failure, readiness timeout) via `killTree` from `daemon-children.js`, in a finally block, and use `freePort` + `--strictPort` so a port collision refuses loudly instead of silently driving somebody else's server.
